overall: Atlanta is warming steadily through midday, with the running max hitting 73.4°F by noon and a strong positive velocity of +3.0°F/hr still driving temperatures upward. The morning started slowly (64.4°F at 7am, only +0.5°F gain to 9am), but heating accelerated sharply after 10am. Dewpoint at 55.4°F and winds at 11.5 mph are modest but could act as a modest cap on peak afternoon temperatures.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show a meaningful spread of ~2.8°F — GFS is the bullish outlier at 78.0°F, while ECMWF comes in at 75.2°F and NBM splits the difference at 76.1°F. The ensemble signals are low-conviction (Tier 4/Avoid) for the 78-80°F range at just 21% and 9%, suggesting the upper end of the GFS forecast is unlikely to verify.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 73.4°F at noon and +3.0°F/hr velocity, meaningful additional warming is likely into the early afternoon, but the rate should taper as peak heating passes around 3-4pm ET. Weighing the model blend (average ~76.4°F), the low ensemble confidence above 78°F, and the modest wind/dewpoint environment, the daily high is most likely to land in the 76-77°F range. Confidence is moderate — the GFS upside to 78°F is possible but the cooler ECMWF/NBM guidance and weak ensemble signals above 78°F argue against chasing the high end.
